title: Global Economics & Trade
completion_message: ¡Magnífico! Entender términos como 'GDP', 'Inflation', 'Tariffs' y 'Supply Chain' te permite leer el Financial Times o The Economist con soltura y discutir el impacto macroeconómico en tu empresa.

parts.visual:
Términos Macroeconómicos: 
- GDP (Gross Domestic Product): Producto Interno Bruto (PIB). El valor total de los bienes producidos en un país. 
Ej: The country's GDP grew by 3% this year. 
- Inflation (Inflación): El aumento general de precios. 
Ej: High inflation reduces consumer purchasing power. 
- Interest rates (Tasas de interés): El costo de pedir dinero prestado. 
Ej: The central bank raised interest rates to fight inflation.
parts.audio: Macroeconomic terms. G D P stands for Gross Domestic Product, which is the total value of goods produced and services provided in a country during one year. For example: The country's G D P grew by 3% this year. 'Inflation' is a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money. For example: High inflation reduces consumer purchasing power. 'Interest rates' represent the cost of borrowing money. For example: The central bank raised interest rates to fight inflation.

parts.visual:
Comercio Internacional: 
- Tariff (Arancel): Un impuesto sobre bienes importados o exportados. 
Ej: The government imposed heavy tariffs on imported steel. 
- Supply chain (Cadena de suministro): La red entre una empresa y sus proveedores. 
Ej: The pandemic severely disrupted the global supply chain. 
- Subsidy (Subsidio): Dinero dado por el gobierno para ayudar a una industria. 
Ej: The agricultural sector receives massive government subsidies.
parts.audio: International Trade. A 'Tariff' is a tax or duty to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports. For example: The government imposed heavy tariffs on imported steel. The 'Supply chain' is the sequence of processes involved in the production and distribution of a commodity. For example: The pandemic severely disrupted the global supply chain. A 'Subsidy' is a sum of money granted by the government to assist an industry or business. For example: The agricultural sector receives massive government subsidies.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término económico o de comercio correcto.

questions.question: The total value of everything produced in the country is called the ____. (PIB).
questions.explanation: GDP = Gross Domestic Product (Producto Interno Bruto).

questions.question: When prices rise and money loses value, the country is experiencing ____. (Inflación).
To make borrowing money more expensive, the central bank raised the ____ rates. (Tasas de interés).
A tax placed on goods coming from another country is called a ____. (Arancel).
The network of suppliers, factories, and logistics companies is called the ____ chain. (Cadena de suministro).
The government provided a financial ____ to help farmers keep prices low. (Subsidio).
questions.explanation: Subsidy = subsidio, ayuda financiera del gobierno.

questions.question: When a country imports more than it exports, it has a trade ____. (Déficit).
When a country exports more than it imports, it has a trade ____. (Superávit).
Due to the economic crisis, the country went into a deep ____. (Recesión).
questions.explanation: Recession = recesión (caída del PIB durante dos trimestres consecutivos).

questions.question: The national ____ is the total amount of money that a country's government has borrowed. (Deuda pública).
questions.explanation: National debt = deuda nacional / deuda pública.

questions.question: We need to analyze the ____ and demand for this new product before manufacturing it. (Oferta y demanda).
questions.explanation: Supply and demand = oferta y demanda.

questions.question: The rate at which one currency can be traded for another is the ____ rate. (Tipo de cambio).
questions.explanation: Exchange rate = tipo de cambio (ej. USD a EUR).

questions.question: Raw materials like oil, gold, and wheat are traded as ____. (Materias primas / Commodities).
questions.explanation: Commodities = materias primas básicas que se negocian en los mercados.

questions.question: A sudden, rapid decrease in the value of a currency is called a ____. (Devaluación).
The government imposed a trade ____ on the country, forbidding any commercial exchange. (Embargo).
questions.explanation: Trade embargo = embargo comercial (prohibición de comerciar con un país).

questions.question: Because of inflation, the ____ power of the average worker has decreased. (Poder adquisitivo).
To protect local industries from foreign competition, governments use ____ measures. (Proteccionistas).
The index that measures the average change in prices paid by consumers is the ____. (IPC).
questions.explanation: CPI = Consumer Price Index (Índice de Precios al Consumidor o IPC).

questions.question: A situation where inflation is high, economic growth rate slows, and unemployment remains steadily high is called ____. (Estanflación).
The central bank uses ____ policy, adjusting interest rates to control the economy. (Política monetaria).
questions.explanation: Monetary policy = política monetaria (controlada por el banco central).

questions.question: Gross Domestic Product is abbreviated as ____.
General price increase is called ____. (Inflación)
A tax on imports is a ____. (Arancel con T)
The ____ chain was disrupted. (Cadena de suministro)
Government financial help is a ____. (Subsidio con S)
A trade ____. (Déficit con D)
A trade ____. (Superávit con S)
Economic ____. (Recesión con R)
The ____ rate. (Tipo de cambio con E)
Purchasing ____. (Poder adquisitivo con P)
